q: How long before payments API calls time out?
a: Client requests to the payments API time out after 10 seconds.

q: What do I need to add a new package?
a: Put a short note in the PR covering why it's needed, its licence, and its size.

q: Where do I justify a new npm dependency?
a: In the PR itself: a short note giving why, licence, and size.

q: Why put the ticket ID in branch names?
a: So the tracker links branches automatically.

q: How should I style new components?
a: Write component styles with CSS modules.

q: Can I add a new SCSS file?
a: No, no new Sass files; use CSS modules instead.

q: Why did we move away from Sass?
a: To drop the Sass build step; component styles now use CSS modules.

q: Does the old CSS approach still apply?
a: No. This replaces CSS approach (old): CSS modules, no new Sass files.

q: How many approvals does a PR need?
a: Two approvals are required to merge.

q: Does the module owner have to sign off?
a: Yes, one of the two required approvals must come from the module owner.

q: Why did review requirements get stricter?
a: A bad migration slipped through, so merges now need two approvals, one from the module owner.

q: When does the DB backup run?
a: Every night at 02:00.

q: How long do we retain backups?
a: Backups are kept for 30 days.

q: Why did we change the backup schedule?
a: After we lost four days of orders; now nightly at 02:00, kept 30 days.

q: What time zone do we store dates in?
a: Store dates in UTC as ISO 8601.

q: How should timestamps be shown to users?
a: Show dates in the user's time zone; storage stays UTC in ISO 8601.

q: Which date string format do we save?
a: ISO 8601, stored in UTC.

q: What should a user-facing error say?
a: It says what happened and what to do next.

q: How do I write a good error popup?
a: Explain what happened and what the user should do next, never a stack trace.

q: How should I name a feature flag?
a: Use ff_<team>_<feature>.

q: Do new features need to ship behind a flag?
a: Yes, every new feature ships behind a flag named ff_<team>_<feature>.

q: What goes into an outage writeup?
a: A timeline and follow-ups, written blameless within two working days.

q: What port does the web app use locally?
a: The web app runs on port 3000 in local development.

q: Which port is the backend on in dev?
a: The API runs on port 8080 in local development.

q: What's localhost for frontend vs API?
a: Web app on port 3000, API on port 8080 locally.

q: What log level does prod use?
a: Production logs at info level.

q: Can I turn on debug logs in production?
a: Only behind a feature flag, and for one hour at most.

q: Why did we change the logging rules?
a: Logs filled the disk, so production moved to info level with time-limited debug.

q: Which Node version should services use?
a: Build and run every service on Node 22.

q: When did we bump the Node runtime?
a: The switch to Node 22 happened in the October upgrade.

q: How long is an on-call shift?
a: On-call rotates every week.

q: When does on-call handover happen?
a: Handover is on Monday at 10:00.

q: Why did we stop monthly on-call?
a: It changed to weekly because a month was too tiring.

q: How fast must the home page load?
a: The home page must load in under 2 seconds on a mid-range phone.

q: What device is the perf target measured on?
a: A mid-range phone; the home page must load in under 2 seconds.

q: How do we cut a release?
a: Ship only from a tag on main; CI builds and publishes the release.

q: Who publishes the release build?
a: CI builds and publishes the release from a tag on main.

q: Why must releases come from main tags?
a: Because a hotfix shipped from a feature branch skipped the tests.

q: How do I run unit tests?
a: Run the unit tests with make test.

q: How do I run integration tests?
a: Run make test-int, with Docker running.

q: Do integration tests need Docker?
a: Yes, make test-int needs Docker running.

q: Where do developer docs live?
a: Developer docs live in the docs/ folder of each repo, not in the wiki.

q: Which folder holds a repo's engineering docs?
a: The docs/ folder inside each repo holds its developer docs.
